item.title: Henry Winkler opens up about the unexpected career he considered before becoming an actor
item.description: Henry Winkler almost studied to become a child psychologist before transitioning into a career as an actor and finding fame as Fonzie on "Happy Days."
item.content:encoded:
Henry Winkler is opening up about what career path he would have chosen had he not gotten into acting.

During a recent interview on the "You Could Make This Beautiful" podcast, the 80-year-old actor shared that he almost decided to become a child psychologist, because he was so dyslexic that "whatever I could do, with the least amount of education" was what he wanted to do.

"I understand children. I’m able to listen, I think, to children. I’m interested in what they have to say and how they are. I marvel at their prowess in the universe," Winkler said. "Yes, I would work with children."

Ultimately, the actor found fame playing Arthur "Fonzie" Fonzarelli on "Happy Days" from 1974 to 1984, a role which earned him three Emmy Award nominations.

'HAPPY DAYS' STAR HENRY WINKLER FILMED HIS FIRST-EVER NUDE SCENE AT 79

The actor has spoken about his lifelong struggle with dyslexia many times in the past and about how he learned to manage it in his career.

"Destiny is very strange, because I've chosen a profession that is so unbelievably difficult, not only to survive in, but to participate in for me," he told "PBS News Weekend" in November 2023. "When we were doing 'Happy Days' or any table read, which is the whole cast all the producers, the directors, everybody on the crew listening, for the first time to the script. I couldn't read off the page. And it was embarrassing. It was humiliating. I covered it with humor."

To manage the obstacles dyslexia presented in his career, Winkler explained that he would "literally read one word at a time" and ask for the script to be delivered to him ahead of time so that he would "almost memorize it" so that by the time it came to the table read, "I could read it with a flow."

While the actor had struggled with dyslexia his whole life, he didn't receive a diagnosis until he was in he was 31, and his young stepson was diagnosed with it, telling PBS that he was initially angry after getting a diagnosis.

"I was because I was humiliated. I was constantly browbeaten. I was punished, grounded for most of my life," he said. "Then the next stage was all right, so I have this thing. Now I have to learn to negotiate it because it doesn't go away. It is the wiring in your brain."

He later learned to reframe the situation and began thinking, "maybe I would not be sitting in this chair" if he hadn't gone through "the challenge to constantly work through that made my tenacity, like steel."

Following his time on "Happy Days," Winkler continued acting, introducing himself to a younger audience in the 1998 movie, "The Waterboy," alongside Adam Sandler.

He then appeared in TV shows such as "Arrested Development," "Parks and Recreation" and "New Girl," before landing a starring role in the hit HBO Max show, "Barry," playing Gene Cousineau, an acting coach who finds himself befriending an assassin.

The role earned him his first ever Emmy Award win in 2018.

"Be yourself, be honest about your ability, prepare so that you are not a flash in the pan," he said backstage after his win, per Variety.

"When I first started here in Hollywood … I thought of myself as a tree or sapling. I planted. I wanted to grow and be strong until I couldn’t do this anymore. And what a great tree it is."

item.title: Roger Miller given stark choice after getting caught stealing: ‘You can go to jail or you can go in the Army’
item.description: Dean Miller says his father joined the Army as a teen after he was caught stealing from a club. The judge then gave him a choice between jail and the Army.
item.content:encoded:
Roger Miller's son is getting candid about why his famous father joined the Army as a teenager.

During a recent interview on the "Drifting Cowboy" podcast, the country music legend's son, Dean Miller, discussed how his father grew up "on a farm with no electricity" and would spend the weekends driving to Amarillo, Texas to play shows at a nightclub in an effort to break into the music industry.

"He would play at this one club, and he was friends with the guy and my dad, as he describes it, was ignorant and didn't know how to break into show business or how to get out of town or what to do with his life," he said.

Dean explained that his dad later had the idea that "if he stole a bunch of stuff from this club, he'd have all he needed to be in show business," leading him to steal equipment and costumes. According to the singer's website, he stole a guitar because he wanted it "so desperately to write songs," and turned himself in the next day.

"The police caught him and the guy that he stole from wrote a letter to the judge and said, 'Please be lenient on this kid. He doesn't know any better. He's a good kid."' And all this stuff," Dean said. "And so they told my dad, 'You can go to jail or you can go in the Army. Your choice.' And he chose the Army."

After joining the Army, Roger was deployed to Korea during the Korean War, which he referred to as the "Korea Clash of '52."

Dean recalled his father telling him that while in Korea, "I just spent the whole time hiding under a jeep and crying."

Ultimately, his time in the Army helped him in his music career, with Dean saying that is where "he met people in music" and was able to get "recommendations to people back home and started coming to Nashville after that."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

It was while he was in the Army that he met his longtime friend and writing partner, Bill Anderson. The two would go on to write many hit songs together, including "When Two Worlds Collide," which became a Top 10 hit.

Roger is often regarded as a major figure in country music, credited for broadening the range of the genre by including elements of pop music in his songs.

Between 1965 and 1966, Roger won 11 Grammy Awards, including best contemporary country album for "Dang Me/Chug-A-Lug," and best country song for "Dang Me" and "King of the Road." He received a total of 18 nominations.

Throughout his career, he also wrote the score for the Broadway musical, "Big River," and the soundtrack for the Disney movie, "Robin Hood." He was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 1995, three years after his death.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Look at Buck Owens or Roger Miller; they're both icons in my eyes," Kacey Musgraves told The Boot in 2018. "Roger Miller was known for his humor, but there was a lot of deep water under those songs, and a lot of meat on those bones. Look at all the places he went: From Broadway to Disney. To me, if you look beyond the box, the whole world is waiting — no matter what you call the music, just be true to what you're doing."

The country music icon died in October 1992 at the age of 56 following a battle with lung cancer.

item.title: Ex-detective who served fraction of 102-year sentence faces new charges after cold case review
item.description: Former Los Angeles vice detective Michael Douglas Brambles, paroled in 2020 under California's elderly inmates law, faces new kidnapping charges.
item.content:encoded:
A former Los Angeles vice detective who was sentenced to 102 years in prison three decades ago for multiple rapes but paroled in 2020, because of a California law was arrested again this week, authorities said.

Michael Douglas Brambles, 77, is charged with kidnapping to commit robbery while personally using a firearm in connection with an alleged robbery and sexual assault, according to the Ventura County District Attorney’s Office.

He also faces several aggravating circumstances, "including that the crime involved great violence, the victim was particularly vulnerable, the manner in which the crime was carried out indicated planning, sophistication or professionalism, and that Brambles engaged in violent conduct indicating a serious danger to society," the district attorney’s office said.

CALIFORNIA SUED OVER POLICY THAT COULD FREE SERIAL KILLERS AS LACI PETERSON'S FRIEND SOUNDS ALARM

Brambles allegedly entered Arabella’s Boutique in Thousand Oaks, California, when a woman identified as SW was closing, pointed a handgun at her, and forced her into the backroom where he tied her hands behind her back and sexually assaulted her.

He is also accused of stealing from the business before he left.

The sexual assault allegations cannot be charged because the statute of limitations has passed.

Shortly after the crime, Brambles was identified as a suspect, but he was already being prosecuted for a string of robberies and sexual assaults.

He was convicted on 26 counts, including 18 armed robberies and multiple sexual assaults.

After being sentenced to 102 years, SW’s case was dismissed, which she agreed with, believing he would spend the rest of his life in prison.

But he was able to apply for parole in 2020 under a California law that allows elderly inmates to apply.

NEWSOM-BACKED LAW LETS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHILD RAPIST SEEK EARLY RELEASE AGAIN AS DA URGES 'STOP THE MADNESS'

At his parole hearing, Brambles denied sexually assaulting any women besides the cases he had already been convicted for in Los Angeles County.

While examining SW’s cold case as part of the federal Sexual Assault Kit Initiative, Ventura County District Attorney’s Office investigators realized he had been paroled.

Brambles was arrested on Wednesday and is being held in Ventura County on $2 million bail.

"A few months ago, when investigators from the Ventura County District Attorney’s Office contacted me, I was shocked to hear not only that this man was walking free, but that he had been out of prison for six years," SW said at a press conference this week. "The justice that I and his other victims deserved was denied when he was only required to serve a fraction of the sentence he earned. I am thankful to have this opportunity now to seek justice for myself and for his other victims."

HOUSE DEMOCRAT BLASTED AFTER EARLY RELEASE LAW FREED INMATES LATER CHARGED WITH MURDER

Brambles faces a maximum sentence of 12 years to life if convicted.

"Without her courage, bravery and resolve to once again face the person who allegedly attacked her, we would not be here today," District Attorney Erik Nasarenko said of SW at the press conference. "Despite the passage of time and the long road ahead, SW is committed to seeing Michael Brambles held responsible for these violent accusations from 32 years ago, and so are we."

item.title: Mets become latest on social media to troll Jayden Daniels amid No 5 jersey feud with LSU
item.description: The New York Mets trolled Jayden Daniels on X after beating the Washington Nationals, joining the viral mockery over his cease-and-desist letter to LSU.
item.content:encoded:
The regular season hasn’t started yet, but Jayden Daniels is already being blitzed.

The New York Mets joined the masses on the internet who have made fun of the Washington Commanders star quarterback for sending a cease-and-desist letter earlier this month to his alma mater, LSU, over the use of his name, image and likeness.

After the Mets’ 4-1 win over the Washington Nationals, who, like the Commanders, are in the DMV area, the Mets took a shot at Daniels on X.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"Stopped at 4 out of respect for Jayden Daniels," the Mets wrote in the viral post.

Daniels, who won the Heisman Trophy with LSU in 2023, and his camp reportedly felt that head coach Lane Kiffin allowing DJ Pickett to wear his No. 5 jersey was "disrespectful." The former LSU star quarterback posted a statement on social media Thursday afternoon about the situation.

"I have been locked in on training camp and that's been my number one focus. I have a lot of gratitude for my time at LSU and I'm proud of what my teammates and I accomplished there," Daniels posted. "Obviously there are issues to be worked out between my team and LSU and my hope is that it will get done privately."

JAYDEN DANIELS TELLS LSU TO KEEP HIS NAME OUT OF ITS MOUTH IN WILD NO. 5 JERSEY FEUD INVOLVING NIL

"My sole personal focus is on Commanders' football. I realize the business of football is unique and I trust this can all be resolved."

While Daniels tried to quell the situation, social media has only come after him as hard as any pass rush he will face this season.

StubHub, a ticketing website, said in a post on X that it will no longer offer tickets in groups of five out of respect for Daniels.

The former LSU star can only hope that by the time the regular season begins, the only blitz he is facing is on the field and not online.

item.title: Indiana Pacers' star Tyrese Haliburton has one major problem with the new NBA schedule
item.description: Tyrese Haliburton questioned why his Achilles return after 16 months won't be on national TV, calling out the NBA schedule on a recent podcast.
item.content:encoded:
The NBA schedule was rolled out this week, and not everyone was happy with how it looked.

One of those people? Indiana Pacers' star Tyrese Haliburton.

It's kind of hard to believe, but the last time we saw Haliburton in action was in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, when he tore the Achilles tendon in his right leg, and the Pacers lost to the Oklahoma City Thunder.

That injury forced the former Iowa State Cyclone — who was one of the biggest stars of those playoffs — to sit out the entire 2025-26 season, but now he's ready for action.

And where will that return happen?

On the road... in New Orleans... and not on national TV.

item.title: Florida middle school teacher admits to years of 'inappropriate' conversations with former student: deputies
item.description: Christian Schneider, a Memorial Middle School teacher, allegedly sent inappropriate messages to a former teenage student since 2023, authorities say.
item.content:encoded:
A Florida middle school teacher was arrested after investigators said he exchanged inappropriate messages with a former teenage student and acknowledged communicating inappropriately with the student since 2023.

Christian Schneider, 31, a teacher at Memorial Middle School, was arrested Friday on charges of three felonies following an investigation by the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office.

Detectives opened a criminal investigation into Schneider on July 28, and learned he had been sending inappropriate messages to a former teenage student at Franklin Middle School, according to the sheriff's office.

KENTUCKY MIDDLE SCHOOL TEACHER ACCUSED OF CROSSING THE LINE WITH STUDENT, ARRESTED UNDER NEW ANTI-GROOMING LAW

Schneider told deputies he had engaged in inappropriate communication with the student since 2023, authorities said.

Authorities have not disclosed the student's exact age, how investigators learned about the alleged communications or further details about the messages.

Schneider faces two counts of solicitation or possession of child sexual abuse material, both second-degree felonies, according to Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office booking records.

He also faces one count of unlawful use of a two-way communications device, a third-degree felony.

HIGH SCHOOL COUNSELOR PLEADS GUILTY TO MULTIPLE SEX CRIMES INVOLVING TEEN SHE WAS MEANT TO HELP

The booking records list July 3 as the offense date for each of the three charges.

Schneider was arrested shortly after noon Friday and booked into custody that afternoon, according to jail records.

Each charge carried a $2,500 surety bond, for a combined $7,500. Schneider was released on surety bond at 2:38 a.m. local time Saturday, jail records show.

"Teachers hold a position of trust that comes with enormous responsibility," said Sheriff Chad Chronister. "When that trust is exploited, it's not just a crime, it's a violation of everything our schools are supposed to stand for. Detectives will continue investigating these cases aggressively, and anyone who abuses their position with a child will be held accountable."

The sheriff's office identified Schneider as a teacher at Memorial Middle School and the teenager as his former student at Franklin Middle School.

The agency did not provide additional details about Schneider's connection to Franklin Middle School or when he taught the student.

The sheriff's office said the investigation remains active and that additional information will be released as it becomes available.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Hillsborough County school district for information about Schneider's employment status and for comment on his arrest.

item.title: Popular beach town cracks down on teens with curfews after fights, underage drinking
item.description: Cape May's new Jersey Shore beach curfew bars unaccompanied minors after 8 p.m. and bans backpacks on the promenade amid underage drinking concerns.
item.content:encoded:
A popular Jersey Shore beach town is following its neighbors’ lead by imposing new restrictions on unaccompanied minors amid concerns about underage drinking, fights and other disruptive behavior.

Cape May’s City Council unanimously approved measures requested by the local police department that bar anyone under 18 from the beach after 8 p.m. unless accompanied by an adult. Unaccompanied minors are also prohibited from public places between 10:30 p.m. and 6 a.m.

ONCE-AFFORDABLE SUMMER ESCAPE ROCKED BY SOARING COSTS AS FAMILIES SHELL OUT THOUSANDS

The Cape May Police Department announced that in addition to the curfews, "backpacks and certain bags/containers are prohibited on the Cape May beaches and promenade" after 8:00 p.m., except those containing necessary medical equipment.

"Several arrests have stemmed from fights and underage drinking," Philadelphia ABC station WPVI-TV reported.

Cape May is a historic seaside resort town at the southern tip of New Jersey, famed for its Victorian architecture. Since 2002, its municipal code has prohibited minors from public places between midnight and 6 a.m. between May and September (and 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. in the off-season).

Officials said the new rules are intended in part to prevent the large-scale youth gatherings that have disrupted other Jersey Shore communities. The ordinances are designed "to help keep our beaches, promenade and community safe," they said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"We really wanted to make sure we didn't become the afterparty to some of the other towns that have already made this move," Cape May Mayor Zachary Mullock told WPVI-TV after the city enacted the new ordinances.

"After 10:30, we all know it's not normally the best stuff that happens, then so to be honest as a parent myself, I think there's a good thing," Mullock added.

Other Jersey Shore communities, including Ocean City, Wildwood, North Wildwood and Seaside Heights, have adopted similar curfews and restrictions.

In May, the City of Long Branch announced it had restored order after an unauthorized pop-up gathering drew several hundred teenagers and young adults to the beachfront.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"The event quickly deteriorated into fights, individuals jumping on parked vehicles and disorder along the boardwalk and surrounding streets," the city announced in a press release.

The response ultimately involved 139 officers from Long Branch and assisting agencies, according to the city. Long Branch enacted an emergency 8:00 p.m. curfew, and officers made six arrests in connection with the incident.

"Pop-up gatherings of this nature have repeatedly disrupted Jersey Shore communities, and Long Branch is prepared to act decisively whenever public safety is threatened," Long Branch business administrator and director of public safety Charles Shirley said at the time.

Cape May Police Chief Dekon Fashaw stressed that the measures aren't intended to discourage young people from visiting the resort town.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"We aren’t against juveniles," Fashaw said. "We are not saying we don’t want them here. While they’re here, we just want them to be responsible."

Mullock said the ordinances appeared to be having an immediate effect.

"Frankly, last night, they were out here, and the report I received is that it worked, and we just had families out here enjoying a pleasant evening," he said.

Some visitors are reportedly supportive of the new measures.

"The thing with Cape May especially, this place kinda shuts down at 10, 10:30. So I mean, people are going to bed, I kind of understand it," Jack McCune, of Yardley, Pa., told WPVI-TV.

"I think that's smart. That's planning ahead," said John Christiansen from Staten Island, New York. "It's really just a few bad kids that cause trouble, so once everyone finds out what they need to do then it's good. What happened to game night?"

item.title: Fauci refuses Senate appearance after invoking Fifth Amendment more than 100 times in COVID probe
item.description: Anthony Fauci's attorney rejected Sen. Ron Johnson's request to testify, arguing a second Senate appearance would amount to political harassment.
item.content:encoded:
Dr. Anthony Fauci on Friday declined a request to voluntarily appear before a second Senate panel, opening another front in Republicans’ investigations into the former public health official’s handling of the COVID-19 pandemic.

An attorney for Fauci rejected the request from Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., chairman of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, arguing that compelling Fauci to testify again after his contentious July 29 Senate hearing would "impermissibly harass or degrade Dr. Fauci for political purposes."

Johnson has been conducting a parallel investigation into Fauci and the federal government’s response to COVID-19, including the safety and efficacy of COVID-19 vaccines.

SEN RON JOHNSON TALKS FAUCI EMAILS, NEW SENATE FILIBUSTER STRATEGY ON 'RUTHLESS'

The refusal comes after Republicans on the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee voted along party lines last week to hold Fauci in contempt of Congress after he invoked his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination more than 100 times during the July hearing.

Committee chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., has sought to send the contempt referral directly to the U.S. Attorney's Office in the District of Columbia, bypassing a full Senate vote.

"It’s a good legal discussion, and we will make those legal points to DOJ in sending the referral over," Paul told Fox News Digital ahead of last week’s contempt vote.

At issue is whether Fauci can invoke the Fifth Amendment after former President Joe Biden issued him a preemptive pardon before leaving office.

CAN FAUCI HIDE BEHIND THE FIFTH? GAME-CHANGING BIDEN PARDON MAY NOT PROVIDE COMPLETE COVER, EXPERTS SAY

Paul has argued that Biden’s pardon removed Fauci’s risk of federal prosecution and therefore undermined his basis for refusing to answer lawmakers’ questions. Fauci and his attorneys have disputed that position.

Paul has spent years investigating Fauci’s role in the government’s response to COVID-19 and has accused the former National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases director of funding "risky" research that led to an alleged lab leak of the COVID-19 virus in China. Paul has repeatedly called for Fauci to be prosecuted.

Johnson’s subcommittee has separately obtained records related to Fauci and the government’s pandemic response. Fox News Digital previously confirmed that the Department of Health and Human Services sent the subcommittee a copy of Fauci’s pandemic-era cellphone.

The broader Homeland Security panel also received more than 1,000 pages of Fauci’s personal diary before his July hearing.

Fox News Digital reached out to Johnson’s office to ask whether he intends to subpoena Fauci following the refusal. Fox News Digital also sought reaction from Paul’s office and asked Fauci attorney David Schertler whether Fauci would comply with a subpoena compelling his testimony.

Fox News Digital's Alex Miller and Elizabeth Elkind contributed to this report.

item.title: JJ McCarthy considered 'unpredictable' as Vikings hand starting QB role to Kyler Murray: report
item.description: A source told CBS Sports that J.J. McCarthy was seen as "unpredictable" within the Minnesota Vikings, factoring into the quick decision to name Kyler Murray starter.
item.content:encoded:
It may not have come as a surprise to people that Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell quickly named Kyler Murray the starting quarterback of his offense over J.J. McCarthy, the team’s 2024 first-round selection.

But a recent report indicates that it’s more than just what happened on the training camp practice field between Murray and McCarthy that may have factored into such a quick decision.

It was last summer when some within the Vikings organization were concerned that McCarthy, who missed his entire rookie season due to a knee injury and struggled with consistency in 2025, was "unpredictable," according to CBS Sports.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

In fact, some believed that Max Brosmer, who was an undrafted free agent added to the quarterbacks room, should’ve been the one under center for Minnesota in Week 1.

That wasn’t the case, but the Vikings made it quite known after watching McCarthy complete 57.6% of his passes and throw 11 touchdowns to 12 interceptions across 10 games – Minnesota went 6-4 over that span – they were in the quarterback market this offseason.

KYLER MURRAY AND JJ MCCARTHY GIVE WILDLY DIFFERENT ANSWERS ABOUT THEIR VIKINGS QB ROOM DYNAMIC

"A franchise quarterback is supposed to be the stability piece of a franchise, like you know what you’re getting every day. But with J.J., you weren’t sure which version you were going to get," the source said to the outlet. "I think he’s just still so young and may not have understood yet what that position fully entails and things like the consistency and day-to-day commitment."

The Vikings landed Murray, the former No. 1 overall pick of the Arizona Cardinals, who moved on from him after a roller-coaster tenure in the desert.

And before they faced the New York Giants for their first preseason bout of the 2026 NFL season, the Vikings came right out and named Murray their starter.

So, what exactly does McCarthy’s future hold as he’s in Year 3 and serving as a backup now? One defensive coach told CBS Sports that "he is talented," though he needs to "learn how to manage a game and not do too much and not do more than what’s required of him." If that happens, perhaps the Vikings, or a different team, can trust him in a starting role.

But that’s the thing: is it too soon to discuss McCarthy playing for a different team already? The Vikings do have a new GM, Nolan Teasley, who is not tied to McCarthy’s selection. That was Kwesi Adofo-Mensah, whom the Vikings fired this past offseason.

There’s also the injury factor that hasn’t allowed McCarthy to really get going after winning a national championship with Michigan and being a top 10 pick to the Vikings. The sample size is only 10 games, and though his quarterback rating was the second worst among signal callers with more than 155 pass attempts, there were some flashes of good quarterback play.

And then there’s his age. McCarthy is only 23 years old and can still grow and develop within the position. But he still has tons to prove.

The only problem is Murray, who has proven more in his career thus far, is someone O’Connell trusts more right now with his offense. And O’Connell knows what works — just look at what he did with Sam Darnold in 2024 while McCarthy was injured throughout the season. Darnold went on to revive his career and ultimately win the Super Bowl with the Seattle Seahawks this past season.

One can’t blame Vikings fans if they believe O’Connell can revitalize Murray’s career, but they certainly will hope so after the announcement was made. Meanwhile, McCarthy will have to keep working and wait for that next moment to prove himself.

In his first preseason work with the Vikings on Saturday against the Giants, McCarthy went 4-of-7 for 34 yards with a sack. Carson Wentz , who is battling for the backup role behind Murray as well, went 6-of-11 for 56 yards with one touchdown pass to Myles Price.

Murray played the opening series for the Vikings, connecting on two of his three pass attempts, including a third-and-7 strike to keep a scoring drive alive.

item.title: Cardinals rookie makes MLB history by hitting a home run in each of his first three career plate appearances
item.description: St. Louis Cardinals rookie outfielder Joshua Báez made Major League Baseball history by hitting a home run in each of his first three plate appearances.
item.content:encoded:
St. Louis Cardinals rookie Joshua Báez’s first career game in the big leagues was something out of a movie.

Báez made Major League Baseball history by hitting a home run in each of his first three plate appearances in the Cardinals' game against the Chicago Cubs on Saturday afternoon at Wrigley Field. The 23-year-old wasted no time in his first-ever at bat, as he blasted the first pitch he saw in his major league career 450 feet to dead center field for a two-run homer to give the Cardinals a 3-0 lead.

Báez pummeled Cubs starter Matt Boyd’s 93-mph fastball and sent the Cardinals’ dugout into a frenzy. The rookie rounded the bases with a smile on his face the entire time.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

His second home run of the day came in the fourth inning, once again off Boyd. Báez worked the count full and then hammered Boyd's 78-mph changeup 382 feet into the left-field seats to give the Cardinals a 4-3 lead.

Báez's third home run also came off Boyd, this time off an 83-mph slider on the outside of the plate. The electrifying rookie hammered the ball 368 feet into the right-field seats for a two-run home run, giving the Cardinals a 6-3 lead. The Cardinals' dugout was in disbelief, with multiple players in awe of Báez's historic feat.

The right-handed hitter homered to all three fields on three different pitches in his first three plate appearances of his career. Báez homered off a fastball in his first at-bat to center field, a changeup to left field in his second at-bat, and a slider to right field in his third at-bat. It was a remarkable display of power in his first career game.

Báez, who led Triple-A in home runs before being called up on Saturday, was batting fifth in the order and playing left field. In Triple-A, the Boston native was putting up massive numbers, hitting .256 with 34 home runs, 90 RBI and 21 stolen bases in 103 games.

The Cardinals drafted him in the second round of the 2021 MLB Draft out of high school. The team hopes he can join JJ Wetherholt, Jordan Walker and Alec Burleson to form a young core the team can build around for a long time.

The Cardinals were not expected to compete this season but have surprised many as they entered Saturday at 61-61 and just 3.5 games back of the Arizona Diamondbacks and Philadelphia Phillies for the final Wild Card spot in the National League.

item.title: Trump backs Republican challenger to oust Letitia James amid ongoing mortgage fraud feud
item.description: President Donald Trump endorsed Saritha Komatireddy to challenge Letitia James, calling the New York attorney general the "WORST" in the country.
item.content:encoded:
New York Attorney General Letitia James has drawn a Trump-backed challenger, with President Donald Trump throwing his "complete and total endorsement" behind Republican Saritha Komatireddy in a bid to oust his longtime political foe.

"It is my Great Honor to endorse America First Patriot, Saritha Komatireddy, who is running to be the next Attorney General of the once wonderful State of New York," Trump wrote in a Friday Truth Social post. "Between Kathy Hochul and the Most Corrupt Attorney General in the Country, Letitia James, it has gone to HELL!"

Trump’s endorsement of Komatireddy, who he nominated to U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York in 2020, comes as he continues pressing for James to be prosecuted over mortgage fraud allegations, adding another front to his years-long feud with the Democratic attorney general who once took him to court.

TRUMP'S JUSTICE DEPARTMENT SUES NEW YORK, OTHER BLUE STATES OVER TUITION FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS

Trump did not mince his words in his criticism of James, who successfully sued Trump and The Trump Organization in 2022, accusing them of fraudulently inflating the value of assets on financial statements to obtain more favorable loans.

An appeals court later wiped out the nearly $465 million financial penalty against Trump, ruling the massive disgorgement award violated the Constitution’s prohibition on excessive fines.

"Letitia 'Peekaboo' James, is considered by many to be the WORST Attorney General in our Country. She is a Complete and Total Disaster, who tried running against Kathy Hochul for Governor, and got less than 1% of the Vote in the Polls, and QUIT, taking many innocent suckers down with her," Trump wrote. "She then went back to her WITCH HUNT against your favorite President, (ME!), and others, yet Murder and other Violent Crime is RAGING OUT OF CONTROL in New York, as People and Businesses flee, in Record Numbers, to other States!"

He contrasted James to Komatireddy, touting her qualifications as Drug Enforcement Administration chief of staff, a former federal prosecutor, and that she clerked for Brett Kavanaugh, who went on to become a Supreme Court justice.

"On the other hand, as your next Attorney General, Saritha Komatireddy will fight tirelessly to Ensure LAW AND ORDER, Grow our Economy, Champion our Law Enforcement and First Responders, Support our Military/Veterans, Advance Election Integrity, Keep our Border SECURE, Stop Migrant Crime, Uphold our Constitution, and Defend our always under siege Second Amendment," Trump wrote.

TRUMP MAY HAVE ENDORSED DARLINE GRAHAM, BUT GOP SENATE HOPEFULS AREN’T BACKING DOWN

Komatireddy, who has been outspoken against James' handling of the state's fraud investigations, thanked Trump for his endorsement.

"I was honored to be nominated to be a federal judge by the President in 2020 and I’m honored to receive his endorsement today. I’m working hard to win the support of all New Yorkers and defeat Letitia James this November," Komatireddy wrote on X.

Fox News Digital reached out to James' campaign for comment.

item.title: Courtney Love reveals secret health crisis that nearly killed her: 'My body just exploded'
item.description: Courtney Love shared that her body "just exploded" during a secret health crisis that left her near death, losing all her hair and dropping to 100 pounds.
item.content:encoded:
Courtney Love is revealing a health battle she kept private for years.

The Hole singer, 62, shared an update about her long-awaited new album, explaining that the record took shape during a period when she was frequently hospitalized and believed it could be her final work.

"I went to England in 2019 and when I went there, you know, my body just exploded," Love said in an Instagram video. "It just exploded. And I was in hospitals a lot. I almost died, I lost all my hair. I was about 100 pounds. And they told me I was going to die, and I didn’t believe them."

KURT COBAIN AND COURTNEY LOVE ATTEMPTED TO ESCAPE 'CRAZINESS' OF FAME

Love did not identify the illness or illnesses she was battling, but said she ultimately recovered after refusing to accept the prognosis she had been given.

The singer connected that determination to a memory from childhood, describing a tendency to challenge what adults told her was true.

"When I was a kid — and I think this record is about this — I used to pattern interrupt the adults," she said. "They’d tell me red was blue, and then I’d see blue, but blue was blue, so now that I gaslight myself that maybe they were right, and red was blue, and then I would see purple, and my head would explode. Like f---ing cope with that s---, right?"

She continued, "I never really lost my ability to see that… red was red. Despite them telling me that red was blue. And so, when they said ‘you’re going to die,’ I just didn’t believe them. And somehow, I got better. I’m healthy, which is amazing."

"I just wasn’t public about being sick. I don’t want to be public. I’m fine now."

The singer said she wants to return to the road and perform again, describing music as essential to her well-being.

Her new album appears to have emerged directly from the period in which she was fighting to recover.

In an Instagram caption accompanying her video, Love explained that when she began making the record, she believed it might be her last.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"I wanted to give you an update on my record. When I made it, I believed this was my last record so I made the record I always wanted to make. I was in the hospital mostly but when I wasn’t all I did was write & record it."

Love also thanked those who worked with her while she was dealing with what she described as trauma.

The project would mark a significant return for Love, who has not released an album since Hole’s 2010 "Nobody’s Daughter."

She closed her message by asking fans for patience as she prepares to return to public life.

item.title: Everyday habit linked to dramatically lower risk of dying from heart disease
item.description: Stair climbing was linked to a 39% lower risk of dying from cardiovascular disease, according to an analysis of more than 480,000 participants.
item.content:encoded:
A simple daily habit may be linked to a dramatically lower risk of premature death, particularly from heart disease — no gym membership required.

People who climbed stairs had a 39% lower risk of dying from cardiovascular disease and a 24% lower risk of dying from any cause than those who didn’t, according to an analysis led by researchers at the University of East Anglia and Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital.

DAD SUFFERS HEART ATTACK DAYS BEFORE DAUGHTER'S WEDDING — THEN DOCTORS MAKE SURE HE WALKS HER DOWN THE AISLE

People who climbed the stairs were less likely to develop major cardiovascular conditions such as heart attack, stroke and heart failure, UEA further reported.

"Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death worldwide — with cases nearly doubling between 1990 and 2019," Vassilios Vassiliou, from UEA’s Norwich Medical School, said in a news release.

After reviewing nearly 1,900 studies, the researchers analyzed data from more than 480,000 people across nine studies, which had a median follow-up period of 14 years. The participants included healthy people and those with a history of heart problems, between the ages of 35 and 84.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

The findings show an association between stair climbing and lower mortality risk, but do not prove that taking the stairs directly causes people to live longer.

Stair climbing is a simple but powerful form of exercise because it requires the body to repeatedly work against gravity. The generally low-impact activity engages multiple muscle groups while providing both cardiovascular and strength-building benefits.

One large study included in the analysis suggested that climbing about six flights of stairs per day may offer the greatest benefit, though researchers said more work is needed to determine the optimal amount.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"Some of the studies we looked at showed that the more stairs climbed, the greater the health benefits," said UEA’s Norwich Medical School researcher Sophie Paddock. "But even small changes had a measurable impact."

According to Vassiliou, more than a quarter of adults worldwide fail to meet recommended activity levels. A sedentary lifestyle, smoking, poor dietary habits and obesity all contribute to cardiovascular disease.

Climbing stairs is a cost-free form of exercise people can fit into their day at home, work and in public places and is a good option for people who don't have much time or easy access to exercise, the researchers said.

"Even brief bursts of physical activity have beneficial health impacts, and short bouts of stair climbing should be an achievable target to integrate into daily routines," Paddock said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The researchers cautioned that stair climbing may not be appropriate for everyone, particularly people with mobility issues or joint conditions.

They published their findings in the American Journal of Cardiovascular Drugs.

item.title: Dolly Parton’s ongoing health battle forces country legend to miss major Dollywood event
item.description: Dolly Parton appeared virtually at Dollywood's new roller coaster opening after her Nashville doctor grounded her travel over dizziness and dehydration.
item.content:encoded:
Country music icon Dolly Parton was forced to miss a major Dollywood event Friday after her doctor advised her to stay in Nashville because of continued "health issues."

The 80-year-old "9 to 5" singer was expected to appear in person at the Tennessee theme park for the opening of its new NightFlight Expedition roller coaster, but she ultimately joined the celebration virtually after her doctor told her not to travel.

"I’m still in Nashville, and I’m sorry about that," Parton told the crowd during a video appearance at the event, according to video shared by the Knoxville News Sentinel.

DOLLY PARTON'S SISTER OFFERS HEALTH UPDATE ON COUNTRY ICON AFTER FANS WORRY OVER HER CALL FOR PRAYERS

"I’m supposed to be there in person, like we planned," she continued. "Now I’ve told you before, all my fans, that I have had a few little health issues. And sometimes I get a little dizzy, and I get dehydrated."

"And I’m dehydrated," Parton, who appeared on-screen wearing fairy wings, told the crowd. "And so my Nashville doctor clipped my wings, saying ‘you ain’t traveling this week.’"

DOLLY PARTON UNABLE TO WRITE NEW SONGS AFTER LOSING HUSBAND OF NEARLY 60 YEARS

"So I guess if your doctor tells you, ‘you ain’t traveling this week,’ you ain’t traveling this week," she continued, explaining that she likes keeping her fans "in the loop" and had promised to update them "on everything."

Fox News Digital has reached out to Parton for comment.

LEANN RIMES CANCELS CONCERTS DUE TO SEVERE ILLNESS, SAYS SHE IS 'TRULY HEARTBROKEN'

Parton’s absence comes as she continues to recover from health problems that have forced her to scale back some of her performance plans.

In May, the country legend announced that she was canceling her planned Las Vegas residency, which had already been postponed from 2025 to September 2026 because of health concerns.

"I'm here to give you an update on a few things going on in my life," Parton said in the video at the time. "First, it is concerning my health. And I have some good news and a little bad news. But the good news is, I'm responding really well to meds and treatments, and I'm improving every day."

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

As for the bad news, Parton acknowledged that she wasn't yet physically ready to perform at the level she expected from herself at the time.

"It's going to take me a little while before I'm up to stage-performance level, because some of the meds and treatments make me a little bit swimmy-headed, as my grandma used to say," she quipped. "And, of course I can't be dizzy, carrying around banjos, guitars, and such on five-inch heels... not to mention all those heavy rhinestone outfits, the big hair, my big personality."

Parton has previously discussed problems involving kidney stones, while also saying her immune and digestive systems had gotten "out of whack" and were being treated. She has repeatedly emphasized that she is improving.

"I have great doctors, and I'm doing really well, and they assure me that everything I have is treatable," she said. "So I'm going with that, and I just want you to know I thank you for standing by me and that I will always love you."

item.title: Cardinals top pick Jeremiyah Love out for a least a week after suffering preseason injury, coach says
item.description: Tyler Allgeier steps into the starting RB role as the Arizona Cardinals manage key injuries to Jeremiyah Love and veteran James Conner this week.
item.content:encoded:
The Arizona Cardinals will be without the No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft for at least a week.

Head coach Mike LaFleur said Saturday that running back Jeremiyah Love suffered an ankle injury during the team’s preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Thursday. Love, despite not having much concern following the game, came into the building on Friday sore.

"He was in great spirits, even Friday," LaFleur said. "But we'll keep him out this week as we let it heal. So, a little bit more sore than we were anticipating."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

When asked how Love’s injury could impact his Week 1 status, LaFleur declined to look further than Saturday’s practice.

"This week and then we'll kind of go from there and reevaluate," LaFleur said. "Honestly, all the focus is on August 15th, Saturday. Here we are in our Tempe block (of practice). We'll kind of reevaluate going into next week. But he will be out this week."

LaFleur said Love will not play in the team’s second preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys next Saturday. Love recorded 11 carries for 58 yards and three catches for 14 yards in the Cardinals’ first preseason game.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

With Love out, Tyler Allgeier will step into the starting role with Bam Knight and Corey Kiner backing him up. Veteran running back James Conner has not yet participated in 11-on-11 drills as he recovers from a right foot injury that forced him to miss 14 games last season.

Unfortunately for the Cardinals, Love is not the only rookie who sustained an injury in the team’s first preseason game. Second-round pick Chase Bisontis, who was in contention for the starting right guard position, tore the MCL in his left knee.

LaFleur said Bisontis will be placed on injured reserve, delivering a huge blow to the Cardinals' offensive line. He will undergo surgery on the injured knee.

item.title: Bernie-backed California House candidate called DEI a ‘social justice-driven duty,’ embraced activist role
item.description: Bernie Sanders-backed California candidate Randy Villegas promoted DEI as a "social justice-driven duty" in his academic writings on community colleges.
item.content:encoded:
A Bernie Sanders-backed California congressional candidate who touts his career as an educator has used the classroom and academia to push diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) initiatives and activist groups, according to his own writings and reports on his work with students.

Randy Villegas is taking on Republican Rep. David Valadao in California’s 22nd Congressional District in a high-stakes Central Valley showdown that could help determine control of the House.

Democrats have made the seat a top pickup target as the nonpartisan Cook Political Report rates the district a "toss-up" and gives the district a razor-thin D+1 partisan lean.

Villegas, a political science professor at College of the Sequoias and Visalia school board trustee, co-authored a 2022 academic paper arguing that DEI is central to the mission of community college educators and describing it as a "social justice-driven duty."

The paper, titled "A Commitment to Teaching, Learning, and Student Advocacy: Community College Careers," was published by the American Political Science Association as a chapter in Strategies for Navigating Graduate School and Beyond.

"At the heart of community college teaching is diversity, equity, and inclusion, and culturally responsive teaching," Villegas wrote. "Community colleges commit to teaching excellence and to a social justice-driven duty to accessibility. Most community colleges have similar institutional characteristics as a result. For example, community colleges are open access institutions. This means that all students are accepted."

COAST GUARD ENDING RACE-BASED ADMISSIONS FOR OFFICER COMMISSIONING PROGRAM UNDER TRUMP DEI CRACKDOWN

Villegas and his co-authors framed diversity and inclusion as a responsibility that extended beyond campus, writing that "a commitment to diversity and inclusion expands from the classroom to the communities in which students live" and arguing that students’ "social and economic realities" should also shape course design.

While the paper pre-dates President Donald Trump’s push to eliminate DEI mandates across the federal government and education system, it sheds light on Villegas’ views on DEI and social justice in higher education.

In his dissertation, "Voices from the Valley of Vulnerability," written for the University of California, Santa Cruz, Villegas identifies himself as a "former community organizer and scholar activist" and makes the case that activism can be part of his scholarly work.

He bats away concerns that activism could affect academic objectivity, arguing that his activism gave him access to information and that his identity and life experiences made his research stronger. He cites scholar Zepeda-Millán, who argued that researchers’ "biases can actually be assets."

MICHIGAN SENATE CANDIDATE ABDUL EL-SAYED DODGES QUESTION ON WHETHER HE STILL SUPPORTS DEFUNDING THE POLICE

Throughout the paper, Villegas described taking part in grassroots activism that included organizing May Day demonstrations, protesting outside an immigrant detention center and working with community groups to advocate for far-left causes.

He argued that schools often failed to sufficiently engage students in politics, describing educational institutions as "anti-political" while praising community organizations for "actively politicizing and socializing youth" and empowering them to become "agents of change."

That push to turn students into political activists went beyond his academia research. In 2018, Villegas helped lead the Central Valley Freedom Summer (CVFS), a program that connected students with community organizations for voter outreach, civic engagement and grassroots organizing. Participants worked on issues including LGBTQ rights, immigration, environmental justice and racial inequality while conducting voter-registration and turnout efforts. Among those groups that teamed up with CVFS was Jakara Movement. In 2020, the group launched a campaign seeking the removal of a statue of Mahatma Gandhi, citing what it described as Gandhi’s "history of anti-Blackness and racism," Breitbart reported.

Some CVFS graduates went on to launch activist groups of their own, including LOUD for Tomorrow, a self-described "queer and trans BIPOC youth-led" organization that has hosted youth drag events across the Central Valley.

600 GROUPS WITH $2B IN REVENUE MOBILIZE 3,000 MAY DAY PROTESTS IN A 'RED-BLUE' ALLIANCE, PROBE FINDS

"Randy Villegas was cooked up in a lab to be the radical left's perfect woke freak. The only thing he cares about is political power and his far-left agenda," Republican National Committee spokesperson Nick Poche told Fox News Digital.

Meanwhile, Villegas did not respond to Fox News Digital’s questions about his statements that educators also wear the hat of a "social activist." Instead, a spokesperson made remarks about incumbent Valadao.

"David Valadao ripped away healthcare and food assistance from Valley families to hand his billionaire buddies a tax break," the spokesperson said in an email. "These desperate attacks won’t hide his toxic record, or the domestic abusers bankrolling his campaign."

The comments appear to refer to Valadao voting in favor of President Donald Trump’s "One Big Beautiful Bill", a sweeping tax and spending package that included roughly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts. Democrats have argued the cuts could cause tens of thousands of people in Valadao’s heavily Medi-Cal-dependent district to lose coverage.

Fox News Digital reached out to Valadao's chief of staff and communications director for comment, as well as Villegas' campaign for clarification on the allegation that "domestic abusers" are financing Valadao's campaign.

item.title: 8 things we learned from Google's Pixel 11 event
item.description: Google's Pixel 11 lineup introduces Magic Capture, HiLight notifications and proactive Gemini features designed to reduce screen time demands.
item.content:encoded:
Google packed a lot into its annual Made by Google event on August 12. We got four Pixel 11 phones, a new Pixel Watch, Google's first finder tag and fresh Pixel Buds features. Yet one theme kept coming through. Google wants its devices to anticipate what you need before you have to ask.

I was especially interested in what these upgrades could change in everyday use. A faster processor sounds nice. A phone that surfaces your flight information when someone texts you about a trip feels much more personal.

If you want to see how much has changed in one generation, take a look back at our coverage of the Pixel 10 event and Google's previous phones, smartwatch and earbuds. Here are the eight things that stood out to me.

Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will explain how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed. You’ll also receive our financial protection checklist, and every registrant will get a link to the class recording afterward.

Reserve your free spot today at CyberGuyLive.com.

The phone lineup includes the Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL and Pixel 11 Pro Fold. All four use Google's new Tensor G6 processor and are designed around its latest Gemini Intelligence features.

The standard Pixel 11 gets a camera bar that is 40% thinner than earlier base-model Pixels. It also has a larger 48-megapixel main camera with 56% more light sensitivity than the Pixel 10. Its 5x telephoto camera now supports up to 30x Super Zoom. The Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL have Google's brightest Pixel displays yet, reaching up to 3,600 nits. Google also says a new display coating provides more than twice the scratch resistance of the previous Pro generation. Their upgraded telephoto camera can reach up to 120x Pro Zoom. All three traditional Pixel 11 models now start with 256GB of storage. Google also carries Pixelsnap magnetic wireless charging into the Pixel 11 lineup, with Qi2 support and faster wireless charging that can reach up to 25W on compatible models. Pixelsnap lets you snap on compatible chargers, stands, grips and other magnetic accessories.

Then there is the Pixel 11 Pro Fold. Google made it almost 10% lighter and about 1 millimeter thinner than the Pixel 10 Pro Fold. A redesigned hinge, new back material and stronger outer display also make it three times more durable than last year's Fold, according to Google's testing. That gives the Pixel 11 family a clearer reason to upgrade beyond AI alone. Google has changed the cameras, durability and charging experience while refining the physical design.

Google is also trying to make switching from an iPhone less painful. Quick Share on Pixel can now send and receive photos and videos with iPhones and MacBooks, while Google says your photos and group chats can move over when you switch.

All four Pixel 11 phones are available for preorder now, including the Google Pixel 11, Google Pixel 11 Pro, Google Pixel 11 Pro XL and Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold. They officially go on sale August 20.

FBI HELPS TAKE DOWN AI PHISHING RING

Google is taking another step toward making Gemini feel less like an app you open and more like something that can help across your phone. Gemini can now handle multistep tasks across more than 40 apps. Pixel 11 can also surface information based on what you are doing. For example, if a friend messages you about an upcoming trip, a card can appear with your booking information and flight status. Pixel can also suggest actions based on your conversation. If you are discussing dinner plans, for example, it may offer a prompt to make a reservation. It can suggest adding an event to Calendar or saving a location to Maps.

Google also introduced Rambler, a Gemini-powered voice input feature. It cleans up natural speech as it transcribes you. That means filler words such as "um" and "ah" do not have to end up in your finished message. That could be one of those small features you quickly start using every day.

Much of this is powered by Google's new Tensor G6 processor. Google says Tensor G6 can process on-device AI tasks up to 3.5 times faster while using up to 3.5 times less energy than the previous generation under its testing.

Google also introduced Sign To Text, which lets Pixel understand American Sign Language through the camera. Users can sign to write, chat or prompt Gemini from the keyboard. Google says the feature can recognize one-handed and two-handed signing along with facial expressions for grammar and tone. It is available for ASL now, with more sign languages planned.

One of my favorite ideas from the event is Magic Capture. Instead of making you concentrate on hitting the shutter at exactly the right second, Magic Capture can analyze around 400 frames during a typical session. It then delivers carefully timed 12-megapixel photos. The feature can also automatically crop or unblur an image. At the same time, it saves video without making you switch camera modes. That could come in handy with kids, pets or anything else that refuses to pose for you.

The hardware gets an upgrade too. Pixel 11 has a new 48-megapixel main sensor that Google says delivers 56% more light sensitivity than Pixel 10. Its 5x telephoto camera can reach 30x Super Zoom. Meanwhile, Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL get an upgraded 48-megapixel telephoto camera. Google says its larger sensor provides 30% more light sensitivity. The Pro phones can reach up to 120x Pro Zoom.

Google says the new Instant Night Sight is four times faster, helping Pixel capture low-light photos without requiring you to hold the phone still as long. There is also a new Camera Looks feature. It lets you choose a visual style before taking the photo. You can select a default look or customize additional styles to suit the shot. If the camera is your biggest reason for upgrading a phone, you may also want to compare the new Pixels with our current top Android phones of 2026 at cyberguy.com.

Remember when phones had little notification lights? Google is bringing that idea back in a much more noticeable way. Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL introduce HiLight. Colored LED lights around the camera flash can glow while the phone is face down.

For example, HiLight uses different patterns to show when Gemini is listening, thinking or responding. You can also assign colors to important contacts so an incoming call gives you a visual clue about who is calling. Google says message notifications from favorite contacts are among the capabilities planned for HiLight later.

I like the thinking here. Phones are very good at pulling us back onto the screen. A quick visual signal could give you useful information without demanding your full attention. The Pixel 11 Pro Fold gets HiLight as well.

With Gemini getting access to more context on your phone, privacy was an obvious question at the event. Google says Pixel gives users visibility into what AI is doing and controls over how their data is used. You can also turn AI features on or off.

Google highlighted several security protections built into Pixel 11. The phone can automatically block many spam calls and texts while warning you about messages or calls that may be scams. Google is also promising seven years of automatic security updates. An upgraded security chip is designed to help protect personal information stored on the phone.

Pixel Watch 5 may be the device I would watch most closely after launch. Google upgraded its GPS and says route tracking can be twice as accurate as previous Pixel Watch generations in difficult environments. The watch also gets 50% more RAM and a faster processor compared with Pixel Watch 4. Then there is Google Health. Pixel Watch 5 introduces Health Guardian features that look for longer-term changes in your wellness. These include monthly summaries involving blood pressure trends, sleep breathing quality and insulin resistance trends. Google says these features are designed for general wellness and are not intended to diagnose or treat medical conditions.

The headline safety feature is Breathing Emergency Detection. It uses the watch's sensors and on-device AI to look for a severe, persistent drop in oxygen saturation. If the wearer becomes unresponsive, the watch can automatically call emergency services and transmit the person's location. There is an important catch for U.S. buyers. Breathing Emergency Detection is currently available on Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5 in select European countries. It is not currently available in the United States. Google says it plans to expand the feature to more countries.

Pixel Watch 5 is available for preorder now and starts at $399 for the 41mm model and $429 for the 45mm version. The watches go on sale August 20.

Google is officially entering the finder-tag business. Pixel Tag is a small tracker for things such as keys, wallets or luggage. It connects to Google's Find Hub network, which includes more than one billion Android devices. That network can help locate an item when your own phone is no longer nearby. When you are close to the tag, Ultra-Wideband with Bluetooth Channel Sounding can provide distance and directional guidance on compatible devices. You can also make the Pixel Tag play a sound. Interestingly, the button on the tag works in reverse too. Press it and you can ring your phone.

Google says the replaceable battery lasts more than one year. The tag carries an IP67 water and dust resistance rating. You can also share a Pixel Tag with up to 10 people. Security matters with any location tracker. Google says Android phones automatically warn you if an unknown tag appears to be traveling with you.

We have covered Google's expanding location tools before. You can read more about Find Hub and Google's Android security protections.

Pixel Tag costs $29 for one or $99 for a four-pack. It is not available for preorder yet. Google says it goes on sale November 11.

WHAT A SCAMMER SEES THE MOMENT THEY GOOGLE YOUR NAME

Google did not replace the Pixel Buds Pro 2. Instead, it announced new software features and a new Olive finish. Google says an upgraded Active Noise Cancellation feature can compensate when the fit or seal changes, helping maintain noise cancellation while you are moving.

Another clever feature connects the Buds with Pixel Watch. Later this year, your Buds will automatically pause audio if your Pixel Watch senses that you have fallen asleep. Google also says Live Translate improvements are coming to Pixel Buds Pro 2 and Pixel Buds 2a later this fall. Pixel Buds Pro 2 are also getting the new Olive color to complement this year's Pixel devices.

The Pixel Buds Pro 2 are available now, with the new Olive color joining the lineup.

Google could have spent its Pixel 11 launch talking mainly about faster processors and brighter displays. Instead, some of the most interesting changes focus on reducing how much attention your devices demand. Magic Capture could make it easier to get the photo without experiencing the entire moment through your screen. HiLight could tell you whether a call matters before you pick up your phone.

I am also watching the Pixel Watch 5 closely. A watch that can automatically call for help during certain breathing emergencies could become an important safety tool.
